instrument_name: Md. Code, Tax-General 10-105 (State income tax rates)
figure_or_rule_carried: Single/MFS/dependent: 2% 1-1,000; 3% 1,001-2,000; 4% 2,001-3,000; 4.75% 3,001-100,000; 5% to 125,000; 5.25% to 150,000; 5.5% to 250,000; 5.75% to 500,000; 6.25% to 1,000,000; 6.50% over 1,000,000. Joint/HoH/surviving spouse: same lower bands, 4.75% to 150,000; 5% to 175,000; 5.25% to 225,000; 5.5% to 300,000; 5.75% to 600,000; 6.25% to 1,200,000; 6.50% over 1,200,000. Additional 2% on net capital gain if FAGI > 350,000 (assessment level, not withholding). Nonresident: rates applied with 10-210 ratio. 6.25/6.50 bands labelled new for 2026 withholding by the Comptroller memo US-MDS5-003.

instrument_name: Md. Code, Tax-General 10-217 (standard deduction)
figure_or_rule_carried: Flat standard deduction 3,350 (single/other), 6,700 (HoH, surviving spouse, joint); indexed for taxable years after 2025-12-31 by IRC 1(f)(3) COLA with 2024 base, increase rounded down to a multiple of 50. Withholding guide 2026 uses 3,400 (consistent with 3,350 + COLA rounded down to 50; the Comptroller COLA figure itself was not read).

instrument_name: Md. Code, Labor and Employment 3-413 (State minimum wage)
figure_or_rule_carried: State minimum wage 15.00/h from 2024-01-01 for all employers (small employer <=14 employees also 15.00 from 2024-01-01); greater of federal or State; employees under 18 may be paid 85% of the State minimum (12.75). No automatic indexation in the text.

instrument_name: Md. Code, Labor and Employment 3-415 and 3-420 (overtime)
figure_or_rule_carried: Overtime 1.5x usual hourly wage for hours over 40 per workweek; no daily overtime. Over 60 h/week for FLSA-exempt agricultural employees; over 48 h/week for bowling establishments and non-hospital residential care institutions. Exemptions: 49 USC 10501 carriers, DOT-regulated drivers, auto/farm-equipment dealers' mechanics and salespersons, taxicab drivers, seasonal amusement, nonprofit theatre and similar.

instrument_name: Md. Code, Labor and Employment 3-419 (tip credit)
figure_or_rule_carried: Tipped employee (>30/month in tips, informed, keeps tips; pooling allowed): tip credit may not exceed the minimum wage less 3.63, i.e. minimum cash wage 3.63/h (at 15.00: maximum tip credit 11.37). Commissioner regulations require restaurant employers using the tip credit to give a wage statement showing the effective hourly tip rate.

instrument_name: Md. Code, Labor and Employment 3-502 (pay frequency, method of payment, SSN)
figure_or_rule_carried: Regular pay periods; pay at least every 2 weeks or twice a month (administrative, executive, professional may be paid less often); payday on a nonworkday -> preceding workday; pay in US currency or check convertible at face value; direct deposit only with employee authorization; debit/pay card only if authorized and fees disclosed in writing in at least 12-point font; employer may not print the employee's SSN on the check, attachment, direct-deposit notice or card-credit notice (governmental units included).

instrument_name: Md. Code, Labor and Employment 3-503 (deductions from wages)
figure_or_rule_carried: No deduction unless court-ordered, expressly authorized in writing by the employee, allowed by the Commissioner (full consideration received), or made under a law or regulation.

instrument_name: Md. Code, Labor and Employment 3-505 (final pay; accrued leave)
figure_or_rule_carried: All wages due on or before the day the employee would have been paid had employment not ended (same rule for discharge and resignation). Accrued leave must be paid unless the employer has a written policy limiting payout, notified the employee at hire under 3-504(a)(1), and the policy denies payout.

instrument_name: Md. Code, Commercial Law 15-601.1 (wage attachment exemption)
figure_or_rule_carried: Exempt from attachment: greater of 75% of disposable wages or 30 x State minimum hourly wage x number of weeks in which the wages were earned (30 x 15.00 = 450.00 per week), plus any medical insurance payment deducted; computed per pay period. Uses the State minimum wage (more protective than CCPA 30 x 7.25 = 217.50).

instrument_name: Md. Code, State Finance and Procurement 17-202 (prevailing wage scope and threshold)
figure_or_rule_carried: State prevailing wage does not apply to public work contracts under 250,000 or to federally funded parts covered by Davis-Bacon; applies to TIF-bond funded construction where authorized; applies to mechanical systems service contracts above the SCA threshold (41 USC 6702(a)(2)).

instrument_name: Md. Code, Labor and Employment 3-1301 to 3-1305 (Healthy Working Families Act: earned sick and safe leave)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers with 15+ employees (average monthly headcount of preceding year, all employees counted): paid ESSL at normal wage rate (tipped: not more than minimum wage); 14 or fewer: unpaid ESSL. Accrual at least 1 h per 30 h worked; employer may cap: earn 40 h/yr, use 64 h/yr, balance 64 h, no use in first 106 calendar days, no accrual in a 2-week period with <24 h (1-week: <24 h over current+prior period; semimonthly: <26 h). FLSA-exempt assumed 40 h/week (or normal week if less). Front-load allowed (then no carry-over); carry-over up to 40 h. Rehire within 37 weeks: reinstate unused balance unless paid out. No payout at termination required (3-1304(j)); signed agreement allows recovery of advanced leave from final pay. Excluded: <12 h/week regular, under 18 at start of year, agricultural sector, certain temp-agency and as-needed health/human services workers, construction CBA waiver. 3-1305(f): each time wages are paid, employer gives written statement of available ESSL (online system allowed). Local laws enacted after 2017-01-01 preempted; pre-2017 local laws (Montgomery County) may be amended.

instrument_name: Maryland FAMLI - Make contributions (re-read 2026-11-02)
article_or_section: Calculating contributions; Small employer discount; Collecting and making contributions
figure_or_rule_carried: No 2026 contribution. Rate 0.9% of wages up to the Social Security wage cap for wages paid 2027-01-01 to 2027-12-31, split 0.45% employer / 0.45% employee; employer may withhold up to 50%; fewer than 15 employees (counted inside and outside MD under one EIN; 2027 per quarter from wage and hour reports, from 2028 4-quarter average) remit only the employee share (small employer discount). Statutory ceiling 1.2%; from November 2027 the rate for the next year is announced annually. Coverage: all employees in positions localized in Maryland (UI localization), no opt-out. Deduct in the regular pay cycle; if pay too small, up to six pay periods to collect. Quarterly remittance with wage and hour report via paidleave.maryland.gov, due last day of month after quarter; first due 2027-04-30. Benefits from 2028-01-01, up to 12 weeks, up to 1,000/week (home page).

instrument_name: Maryland Department of Labor, Minimum Wage and Overtime Law (ESS) incl. Howard, Montgomery and Prince George's County minimum wages
authority: Maryland Department of Labor, Division of Labor and Industry
article_or_section: Maryland Minimum Wage; Tipped Employees; County Minimum Wage Laws
figure_or_rule_carried: State 15.00/h; under 18: 85%; tipped cash wage 3.63 with Tip Credit Wage Statement for restaurants. Howard County from 2026-07-01: 16.00 all employers. Montgomery County from 2026-07-01: 18.00 (51+ employees), 16.50 (11-50, and 501(c)(3)/Medicaid home-care with 11+), 15.95 (10 or fewer); indexed each July 1 by CPI-W Washington-Baltimore of prior calendar year; excludes under-19 working <=20 h/week; 85% for under-20 for first 6 months; tipped cash wage 4.00. Prince George's County from 2026-07-01: 15.30 all employers. Overtime: 40 h; 48 h bowling/non-hospital residential care; 60 h agriculture. Exemption lists for minimum wage and overtime.

instrument_name: Maryland DOL Division of UI, Employer Wage File Interface File Specifications (CSV, XML, EFW2, ICESA), updated 2026-04-20
authority: Maryland Department of Labor, Division of Unemployment Insurance
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly UI wage report filed in BEACON (online entry or upload; SFTP on request) in CSV, XML, EFW2 or ICESA; one employer and one quarter per file. Currency fields: digits only, cents with no decimal point (59.60 = 5960), zero-filled. SSN 9 digits. Adjustment codes 00-10 (00 original ... 04 wrong state ... 10 other with description). CSV wage record: record type 2, SUI account, reporting period MMYYYY (last month of quarter), SSN, first/middle/last name, gross wages subject to UI, out-of-state taxable wages paid for the year (optional), hours worked in quarter (optional), 12th-of-month employment flags. Report and tax due within 1 month after quarter end; late report penalty 35, interest 1.5%/month (tax-rate page US-MDP9V-001). XML sample file saved.

instrument_name: Md. Code, Labor and Employment 8-626.1 (new hire reporting)
figure_or_rule_carried: Within 20 days of the date the employee commences work, report to the Secretary: SSN, name, address, date of employment, employer name and address, starting wage, whether employer health insurance is provided, FEIN, State UI account number. By mail, magnetically/electronically or other means; electronic twice-monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart; multistate electronic reporters may designate one state and must name it to the Secretary. Penalty: written warning first, then 20 per month (500 if conspiracy). Registry portal mdnewhire.com (Employer Services Portal; FAQ page returned 403).

instrument_name: Md. Code, Labor and Employment 8-202 (UI covered employment: localization)
figure_or_rule_carried: Covered if performed in MD (incl. federal land, interstate commerce) or deemed by approved reciprocal election. Partly-in-MD work covered in its entirety if out-of-state work is incidental; or not incidental anywhere but base of operations, or else place of direction/control, is in MD; or employee is an MD resident and no part is performed in the base/control state (standard uniform localization test). Also covered: work directed from MD performed in any state/VI/Canada not insured elsewhere; vessel/aircraft crews operated from MD; US citizens abroad for an American employer with US principal place of business in MD.

instrument_name: Md. Code, Labor and Employment 8-206, 8-207, 8-208, 8-209, 8-212, 8-220, 8-221, 8-222 (UI: employment not covered / special categories)
figure_or_rule_carried: Not covered: booth-renting barbers/cosmetologists/nail technicians, direct sellers, newspaper distributors, messenger drivers and taxicab drivers meeting written-agreement tests (8-206); agricultural work unless employer paid >=20,000 cash wages in a quarter or employed >=10 workers in 20 weeks (current/preceding year), crew-leader rules (8-207); churches and church-controlled organizations, ministers and members of religious orders; <50/quarter for 501(a)/521 exempt orgs (8-208); commission-only insurance producers, real estate salespersons (to federal extent), yacht salespersons (8-209); federal government and foreign governments; for State/local government: elected officials, legislators, judges, National Guard, emergency temporaries, major policymaking posts, advisers <=8 h/week, election workers <1,000/yr (8-212); full-time students at seasonal camps <13 weeks, students working at their own school (and advised spouses), credit co-op work-study programs certified by the school (8-220); federally assisted work-relief participants (8-221); per-study paid research test subjects outside nonprofit/government (8-222). Domestic-service rule section not located in this pass.

instrument_name: Maryland Employer Withholding Guide, effective January 2026 (revised December 2025): percentage method parameters, filing categories, exclusions (full re-read)
figure_or_rule_carried: Complements US-MD-P5-1-001 (same file). Formula: wages - standard deduction - exemptions x per-period exemption, then county table. Annual exemption 3,200 (weekly 61.54, biweekly 123.08, semimonthly 133.33, monthly 266.67, quarterly 800, daily 8.77); standard deduction 3,400 flat (weekly 65.38, biweekly 130.76, semimonthly 141.66, monthly 283.33, quarterly 850, daily 9.31: guide truncates, not rounds). Tables ignore the 2/3/4% bands (start at 4.75%). Ten local tables (2.25, 2.40, 2.65, 2.75, 2.85, 3.00, 3.05, 3.10, 3.20, 3.30): use the table that equals or slightly exceeds the county rate. Combined rate = state band + local; e.g. 3.30 table single annual 8.05% to 100,000, then 8.30/8.55/8.80/9.05/9.55/9.80%; lump-sum annual bonus at 6.50% + county top local rate (9.80% at 3.30). Nonresident (nonreciprocal state): state + special 2.25%, no local; MD residents working in DE/nonreciprocal states: Delaware table (3.30% flat in the extract). No withholding below per-period floors (weekly 96, biweekly 192, semimonthly 208, monthly 417, daily 13.70, annual 5,000). Single/student low-income exemption thresholds (annual 15,750 under 65 / 17,750 65+). Not withheld: domestic service in a private home, ministers/religious orders, nonresident seamen, employees paid <5,000/yr. No certificate: withhold as one exemption. Filing categories: accelerated (>=15,000 prior year and >=700 accumulated: within 3 business days of pay date), monthly (>700 in a quarter: 15th of following month), quarterly (<700/quarter), seasonal, annual (<250/yr, by 31 January). MW506 via Maryland Tax Connect; MW508 + W-2 by 31 January; records 3 years; penalty up to 25%. Gambling >5,000: 9.50% resident / 8.75% nonresident; rollover distributions 7.75%.
